app.name: Camhive
app.tagline: Your cameras. Your footage stays home.
app.cloudDown: The Camhive cloud cannot be reached. Hives on your network keep working with your stored access; sharing, invitations and sign-in need the cloud.

auth.resetSent: If that e-mail has an account, a reset link is on its way (valid for one hour).

auth.registerIntro: Free for one hive. No card needed.

home.heroText: Camhive records your IP cameras on a computer in your home. Watch live and recorded video from anywhere and share access with your family, while every recording stays on your own disk.
home.f1Text: Footage is recorded to your own disk and is never stored in the cloud.
home.f2Text: Direct, encrypted peer-to-peer video on your phone or laptop, at home or on the go.
home.f3Text: Give family members access to single cameras, as viewer or operator, for as long as you like.
home.privacy: No cloud recording. No traffic limits. Recording keeps going even when the internet is down.

transport.title: Connection
transport.liveNote: Live video always travels peer to peer over WebRTC (through our TURN relay only when your network blocks direct connections). This path is for recordings, exports and settings.

path.address: Direct on your network, by address

transport.rebindTitle: Your router may block the local name.
transport.rebindHelp: Many routers (Fritz!Box, pfSense, Pi-hole) refuse public names that point to local addresses. Everything works through the relay; for direct access add this domain to your router's DNS rebind exceptions:
transport.lnaNote: Chrome asks once for permission to reach devices on your local network; allow it to keep the direct path.
transport.removeHelp: Frees the hive slot of your plan at once. The hive is disconnected from the cloud and cannot reconnect; recordings stay on it. To use it again, run `hive claim` on it and claim it anew.
transport.confirmRemove: Remove hive “{{name}}” from your account? Its recordings stay on the device.

cameras.streamUrlInvalid: Enter an address that starts with rtsp:// or rtsps://, without user and password.
cameras.scanHint: Asks every ONVIF camera on the hive's network to answer (about 3 seconds).

plan.upgradeSoon: Paid plans arrive with card payments shortly after the beta; until then plans are assigned by us and promo codes work.

deletion.title: Delete recordings
deletion.help: Remove footage from this hive's disk now, for example when someone filmed asks for it. Deleted footage cannot be recovered.
deletion.includeExports: Also delete exports of this footage
deletion.rounded: Recordings are stored in files of a few minutes; files that touch the range are deleted whole, so the span can be a little wider than you chose.
deletion.pendingNote_one: {{count}} file still being recorded will be deleted within minutes, once it is closed.
deletion.pendingNote_other: {{count}} files still being recorded will be deleted within minutes, once they are closed.

localLogin.title: Sign in on your network
localLogin.intro: Camhive cannot reach this hive right now, but the hive answers on your network. Sign in with the local username and password you set up for emergencies.
localLogin.banner: Signed in locally on your network. Live video, recordings and camera settings work; sharing, members and your plan need Camhive. The local sign-in ends after an hour or when you close this tab.
localLogin.settingsHelp: If Camhive cannot be reached and your offline access has run out, you can still sign in to this hive on your home network with a username and password that only the hive knows. It is off until you set it up.
localLogin.passwordHint: 10–256 characters, not the username. Stored on the hive only, as a hash; never sent to Camhive. Saving ends local sessions that are signed in.
localLogin.locked_one: Too many failed sign-ins. Try again in {{count}} minute.
localLogin.locked_other: Too many failed sign-ins. Try again in {{count}} minutes.
localLogin.lockedUnknown: Too many failed sign-ins. The hive blocks local sign-ins for up to 15 minutes; try again later.
localLogin.unreachable: The hive does not answer on your network right now. Make sure this device is on the same network as the hive.

lanAddress.title: Open your hive by its address
lanAddress.intro: Camhive cannot reach this hive, and its local name does not answer: without the internet the name cannot be looked up. Your browser can still reach the hive at its address on your network.
lanAddress.open: Open the link below. Your browser warns that the connection is not private. Before you go on, check that the warning is exactly this one, for {{name}}:
lanAddress.chrome: Chrome and Edge: the code NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID, and under Advanced: “This server could not prove that it is {{host}}; its security certificate is from {{name}}.” Then choose “Proceed to {{host}} (unsafe)”.
lanAddress.firefox: Firefox: the code SSL_ERROR_BAD_CERT_DOMAIN, and under Advanced: the certificate “is not valid for {{host}}” and is only valid for {{name}}. Then choose “Accept the Risk and Continue”.
lanAddress.safari: Safari: Show Details → view the certificate. It must be issued to {{name}} by Let’s Encrypt (ISRG Root X1 or X2) and must not say “not trusted”. Then choose “visit this website”.
lanAddress.stop: Any other warning (“not trusted”, “self-signed”, an unknown issuer or any other name) means stop: close that tab, something other than your hive answers at this address.
lanAddress.back: When the hive's page says your browser can reach it, come back here and press Try again.
lanAddress.hint: Your router's device list shows it, or `hive status` on the hive's computer.
lanAddress.invalid: Enter the hive's local IP address, for example 192.168.1.23.
lanAddress.stillNot: The hive does not answer at this address yet.

updates.title: Updates
updates.help: The hive installs signed updates itself and goes back to the previous version on its own when a new one does not run well.
updates.manual: Only when I click Update now
updates.saved: Saved. The hive's next update check follows these settings.
updates.requested: Requested: the hive installs it within a minute and restarts. The result appears in the activity log.
updates.lastRolledBack: Version {{to}} did not run well; the hive went back to {{from}} on {{date}}.
updates.needRestart: This hive's updater is older than these settings: changes apply after the hive's service restarts (sudo hive restart). The next update brings a newer updater only with a package install.

unsupported.dev_build: This is a development build: it never updates itself.
unsupported.no_root: This build has no update keys: it never updates itself.
unsupported.no_updater: The hive does not run under hive-updater, so it cannot update itself. Install the package again or run `hive install`.

updates.inWindow: Version {{version}} installs in the update window, {{from}} to {{to}}.
updates.needsPackage: Version {{version}} needs a newer hive-updater than this hive has: install the current package on the hive's computer. Update now cannot install it.

encryption.title: Encrypted recordings
encryption.help: Encrypts the recordings on the hive's disk, so nobody who takes the disk can play them. After every restart of the hive you unlock them with your passphrase; until then the hive keeps recording and live view works.

state.locked: On and locked: recordings play again once you unlock them.
state.unlocked: On and unlocked: recordings play. Lock them to require the passphrase again.

encryption.notSealing: The hive cannot read the archive key, so new recordings are stored unencrypted. Unlock the recordings to fix this.
encryption.warn: Without your passphrase and the key file nobody can play the encrypted recordings, Camhive included: we cannot reset the passphrase. Encryption cannot be switched off again.
encryption.passphraseHint: 10 to 256 characters. Write it down and keep it apart from the hive.
encryption.length: The passphrase must be 10 to 256 characters.
encryption.backupTitle: Encryption is on. Download the key file now.
encryption.backup: Keep the key file apart from the hive, for example on a USB stick or in your password manager. It is useless without the passphrase; with it, the recordings can still be opened if the hive's disk is damaged.
encryption.changed: Passphrase changed. A key file you downloaded before opens only with the old passphrase: download a new one.
encryption.cloudOnly: Switching encryption on, the key file and a new passphrase need a sign-in through Camhive.
encryption.rateLimited_one: Too many wrong passphrases. Try again in {{count}} minute.
encryption.rateLimited_other: Too many wrong passphrases. Try again in {{count}} minutes.
encryption.rateLimitedUnknown: Too many wrong passphrases. The hive blocks unlocking for up to 15 minutes; try again later.
encryption.lockedOwner: The recordings on this hive are locked: the hive restarted or you locked them. Unlock them to play and export footage. Recording and live view go on.
encryption.lockedMember: The recordings on this hive are locked by its owner. Live view still works.
